entities.summary:
Kurino Shin'ichirō (1851-1937) was a Japanese diplomat who played a crucial role in the country's modernization and international relations during the Meiji period.

As a prominent figure in the Japanese government, Kurino Shin'ichirō served as a diplomat and strategist, working closely with other influential leaders to establish Japan as a major world power.

His legacy extends beyond his own lifetime, as the policies and initiatives he championed during the Meiji era continue to shape Japan's relationships with other nations today.

A striking statistic illustrating the impact of Kurino's work is the significant increase in Japan's foreign exchange reserves during his tenure, which rose from ¥100 million in 1890 to ¥1.5 billion by 1900.
